# Publish platform structured logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform-wide structured logging convention: the JSON
log schema, the set of required fields (timestamp, level, component,
namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per supported language (Go,
Python, TypeScript). It is the prerequisite design artifact that every
per-component logging adoption builds against; component adoptions cannot
start until it is published.

## Scope

- Define the JSON log schema: field names, types, and serialization rules for
  structured log records emitted by RHOAI components.
- Specify the required fields and their semantics: timestamp, level,
  component, namespace, and correlation id, including how a correlation id
  propagates across a user request that spans components (Dashboard, serving,
  pipelines).
- Write library guidance for each supported language (Go, Python,
  TypeScript): which logging library to use and how to produce
  convention-conformant records with the required fields populated.
- Publish the convention in a form that adopting teams can consume directly
  (schema plus per-language guidance).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A JSON schema for the structured log record exists and unambiguously
  defines the required fields: timestamp, level, component, namespace,
  correlation id.
- Library guidance exists for Go, Python, and TypeScript, sufficient for an
  adopting team to emit conformant records without further design work.
- The convention defines how a single user request is correlated across
  Dashboard, serving, and pipelines components.
- The convention is published and available to all adopting component teams.
- Given a raw log line from any adopting component, When it is parsed as
  JSON, Then all required fields are present and typed per the schema.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields, and library guidance per language.

# Adopt convention-conformant logging in Dashboard

## Description

The Dashboard (odh-dashboard, the single-pane web console) adopts the
platform structured logging convention so its logs are machine-queryable and
correlatable with serving and pipelines logs via the correlation id. This
directly addresses the support-case pain of correlating one user request
across components.

## Scope

- Update Dashboard logging to emit records conformant to the published
  platform JSON logging convention (TypeScript per the convention's library
  guidance).
- Populate the required fields on every log record: timestamp, level,
  component, namespace, correlation id.
- Propagate/emit the correlation id so a user action in the Dashboard can be
  correlated with the corresponding serving and pipelines activity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the running Dashboard, When any log record is emitted, Then the
  record is valid JSON conforming to the platform convention schema with all
  required fields present (timestamp, level, component, namespace,
  correlation id).
- Given a user action initiated in the Dashboard, When its logs are queried
  by correlation id, Then Dashboard log records for that action are
  retrievable by that id.
- No remaining ad-hoc (plain text / key=value) log output in Dashboard code
  paths covered by this adoption.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs.
